description: KeyCortexController commands are attributed to the authenticated member (R0-09-ID-HARDEN review R09-ST-4 and CR-3; R0-34b review ST-3). Every KeyCortexController handler that hands a user to a service takes it from @CurrentUser() (the principal AuthGuard admitted) through requestActorId; a body or query userId naming someone else is IGNORED (pinned: not refused; the DTOs keep it as an optional string), and with no authenticated user the handler answers 401 instead of running as 'system', 'key_user' or nobody. The KEY settings adapter applies IdentityService.assertBusinessOwner (owner ruling D-11) on the command's actor with its User role before settings.update_business_profile and settings.update_branding: a STAFF or ADMIN (settings:write) command answers 200 with the connector failure shape (result.success false, 'Only the business owner can edit the business profile') and leaves the Business row byte-identical; an OWNER membership and SUPER_ADMIN succeed; Business.ownerId alone does not (D-104, D-116). Run from apps/server against this packet's isolated, migrated database: npx vitest run test/key-cortex-actor-binding.integration.test.ts src/modules/key-cortex/adapters/settings-adapter.service.spec.ts src/modules/key-cortex/key-cortex.controller.spec.ts src/modules/key-cortex/key-cortex-executor.service.spec.ts src/modules/key-cortex/key-cortex-planner.service.spec.ts src/modules/key-cortex/key-cortex-goals.controller.spec.ts --reporter=json --outputFile=.proof/r0-09c-vitest.json, then node ../../scripts/proof-admission/evaluate.mjs --manifest ../../scripts/proof-admission/manifests/key-cortex-actor-binding.json --report .proof/r0-09c-vitest.json. RED-BEFORE (claude/elegant-curie-7azpsb at a230d7fc, tests-first commit 3a6b4076): the real-database suite failed 15 of 22 (execute with body userId=OWNER ran the command as the OWNER; execute with no userId ran as 'system'; the natural-language path parsed and built for the body user; POST query routed its command with userId undefined; rollback named 'system'; batch named the body user for every command; STAFF and ADMIN settings.update_business_profile / update_branding succeeded and changed the row; conscious/stream, conscious/chat and POST sessions wrote CortexSession rows for the outsider named in the request; chat, chat/stream and stream handed the reasoning engine the request user, stream 'key_user' when none; GET sessions?userId=OWNER listed the OWNER's session to a STAFF member; feedback recorded the outsider). The settings-adapter spec failed 9 of 21 and the controller spec 9 of 19. Cases without RED-BEFORE passed before the fix and are controls (AuthGuard 401, BusinessGuard 403 for a member of another business, OWNER and SUPER_ADMIN writes, delegation of the other settings actions). After the red run, three execute cases were changed from an exact list of routed commands to the command plus at most its compensating revert_<action> (the executor's rollbackOnFailure attempt, which runs only once the adapter refuses), every one still for the STAFF member. SCOPE LIMIT at R0-09c (review ST-5 / CR-2), closed by R0-09e-KEY-PLAN-ACTOR below: KEY plans took a body userId (KeyCortexGoalsController handed the planner dto.userId, the planner built each step as plan.userId ?? 'key_cortex', and POST plans/:id/execute took no actor), so a STAFF member naming the OWNER ran plan steps as the OWNER. REVIEW REPAIRS (pkt/R0-09c-KEY-ACTOR-BINDING-repair on 056e9e8d): ST-1..ST-4, a session is the member's who opened it: GET/PATCH/DELETE sessions/:id, GET messages (with or without sessionId), POST chat, GET chat/stream, GET stream, POST conscious/chat, GET conscious/stream, POST feedback and POST personalities/switch hand the session services only one of the authenticated user's own sessions in the guard-checked tenant (KeyCortexController.ownSession): another tenant's session, cached or not, and another member's session are not found (an error event once an SSE stream is committed), GET messages with no sessionId reads the caller's own newest session, and an id naming no session still starts a new session (or records a new feedback row) for the caller. CR-1, settings.remove_team_member and update_role refuse a command whose parameters.userId is not a non-empty string before any lookup, so the executor compensation for a failed add_team_member (remove_team_member with the add's {email, role}) and a command with no target no longer delete or re-role whichever membership Postgres reads first. ST-6, settings.configure_integration applies ModuleScopeGuard's rule on the command actor (connect at write or above from the explicit scope map or else the role defaults; SUPER_ADMIN passes), so STAFF, an ADMIN granted settings:write and an OWNER without a connect grant are refused, as on the HTTP connections routes. RED-BEFORE the repair (the repair tests on 056e9e8d): the real-database suite failed 9 of 34 (every new RED-BEFORE case; in that run the CR-1 compensation deleted a membership, so the ST-6 case was re-run alone on 056e9e8d and failed on the assertion itself, STAFF disconnect success true), the controller spec 5 of 25 (the four new RED-BEFORE cases and the strengthened messages case, which now asserts listSessions(businessId, actor)), and the settings-adapter spec 4 of 27; the positive controls passed. R0-09e-KEY-PLAN-ACTOR (R0-09c review ST-5 / CR-2 and ST-7; pkt/R0-09e-KEY-PLAN-ACTOR on claude/elegant-curie-7azpsb at 77f3aabf): KEY plans act for the authenticated member. POST plans and POST goals/:goalId/plans take the actor from @CurrentUser() (requestActor in key-cortex-goals.controller.ts); a body userId naming someone else is IGNORED, as KeyCortexController does since R0-09c (the DTOs keep it as an optional string), and with no authenticated user the routes answer 401. POST plans/:planId/execute takes the guarded tenant and the principal; KeyCortexPlannerService.executePlan reads the plan in that tenant only (another tenant's plan is 404) and admits, pinned, the plan's creator, the business OWNER (OWNER membership or Business.ownerId) or SUPER_ADMIN; anyone else is 403 before the plan starts. Every step runs as the EXECUTING member, never as the creator named in the row and never as 'key_cortex', so a STAFF member's settings.update_business_profile step is refused by the owner rule exactly as a direct command is, and the OWNER or SUPER_ADMIN running a STAFF plan runs it as itself. A plan run with no member (KeyCortexTriggerService and the query pipeline call executePlan directly) runs a member's plan as that member and only a plan no member created as SYSTEM_PLAN_ACTOR 'key_cortex'. KeyCortexExecutorService.logExecution writes only AiExecutionLog's own columns through the typed client (userId, actor, action, toolName, module, inputSummary, outputSummary, success, errorMessage, durationMs, correlationId) and execute() awaits it, logging a failed write: each execute writes one ai_execution_logs row naming its actor (userId and actor 'user' for a User row; userId null and actor 'system' for a system actor such as 'key_cortex', the actor id kept in inputSummary). RED-BEFORE R0-09e (tests-first commit dd03cb60, source unchanged): the real-database suite failed 11 of 47 (plans written with userId=OWNER from a STAFF body; the STAFF member's plan ran update_business_profile as the OWNER and changed the profile; a plan created with no userId ran as 'key_cortex'; STAFF on the OWNER's plan, STAFF on a system plan and ADMIN on a STAFF plan answered 201 instead of 403; OWNER and SUPER_ADMIN ran a STAFF plan as the STAFF member; no execute, plan step or system-trigger run wrote an ai_execution_logs row), the two new controls passed (another tenant's plan 404, no identity 401). Against the unmodified sources the unit specs failed 20 of 41 (goals controller 9 of 20: every R0-09e case and the three plan cases that now pass the principal; executor 6 of 6; planner 5 of 15: the four RED-BEFORE cases and the system-actor case, which then read the SYSTEM_PLAN_ACTOR export and was split into a behaviour control and an export check). POST plans/:planId/execute keeps Nest's POST default 201. allowAdditionalCases is false: the two it.todo hand-offs R0-09c carried are now cases, and every case of the run is required. R0-09e review repair (branch pkt/R0-09e-KEY-PLAN-ACTOR-repair): ST-1 / CR-1, execute() writes its ai_execution_logs row on every path, the five refusals that return before the connector included (a blocked action, an autonomy-orchestrator deny, a legacy-gate BLOCK, a gate error, approval pending), on POST execute and plan steps alike; ST-2, executePlan claims the plan with one conditional updateMany over RUNNABLE_PLAN_STATUSES (draft, pending, approved, failed, waiting_approval) and answers 409 when nothing was claimed, so a completed plan is not re-run and two concurrent executes run it once (an error after the claim releases a still-running plan as failed); ST-3, fetchApprovalPolicy counts ai_execution_logs by createdAt through the typed client, so the business's BusinessSetting (aiAutonomyLevel, aiAlwaysRequireApproval, the spending limits, the hourly cap) applies, and a business with no aiSpendingThreshold keeps the 1000 threshold the fallback held it to. RED-BEFORE the repair (packet head 703ef000, repair tests only): 22 of 94 failed across the real-database suite and the executor and planner specs.
notes: Out of scope, left to V1-03-KEY-CORTEX-PRINCIPAL (blocked on D-17): autonomy-profile write authority (who may change tiers and the kill switch: PATCH autonomy-profile is still membership-only) and the autonomy orchestrator's use of proposedBy beyond receiving the authenticated id (the suite's orchestrator is a recording stand-in).

GET sessions lists the authenticated user's own sessions (it listed every session of the business when no ?userId was sent, or the named user's). The review repair closes the rest of within-tenant session privacy on this controller: GET messages with no sessionId reads the caller's own newest session, and every handler that takes a session id refuses another member's session (KeyCortexController.ownSession). Sessions written before R0-09c under userId 'system' or 'key_user' are reachable by nobody through these routes.

POST query routes its 'query' name to the module adapter as a command like any other (settings.update_business_profile included); it now names the authenticated actor, so the owner rule applies there too.

KeyCortexLearningService.recordFeedback still matches the cognition memory it rewrites by sessionId alone (key-cortex-learning.service.ts, outside this write set). The controller now refuses feedback on a session that is not the caller's own, which covers conversation sessions; a memory keyed by an id that is not a CortexSession (the tool registry can key outcomes by a correlation id) is not covered by that check.

R0-09e: GET plans/:planId still returns any plan of the guarded tenant to any member (read authority on plans was not in scope; the tenant extension scopes the read). POST plans/:planId/execute still honours a body skipApproval for the executor's own approval policy when the autonomy orchestrator does not require approval (pre-existing; not an actor question).

R0-09e: logBatchExecution (the per-batch aggregate row) and fetchApprovalPolicy's hourly count (where startedAt) still name AiExecutionLog fields that do not exist (traceId, parameters, ... and startedAt), so the batch aggregate row is never written and the policy read falls into its catch (its default policy; not exercised by this suite). Each command of a batch is audited by execute(). KeyCortexLifecycleService.recordExecution writes startedAt too. Outside R0-09e (logExecution only).

W11-D116-PROFILE-OWNER re-pin (owner rulings D-104, D-116, 2026-11-12; not a weakening): the two settings-adapter owner cases are retitled and strengthened. The planner's executePlan owner case (Business.ownerId owner) is outside this packet (W11-D116-KEY-OWNER) and unchanged.
